newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX HUB NATGAS CALLED HIGHER AMID FIRMER CASH.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX HUB NATGAS CALLED HIGHER AMID FIRMER CASH.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Monday, led by talk of firmer cash prices and continuing heat in the West, sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.505 to $2.52 after settling to the upside Friday at $2.503 per mmBtu.
Early Monday cash prices at Henry Hub were talked more than 10 cents higher at $2.49-2.52.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at the new contract high of $2.53 and then at $2.56 and $2.595. Support was seen at $2.48 and then at $2.34, $2.30 and $2.25-2.27.

In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded almost 15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.30s. Midcon pipes slipped a similar amount to the mid-$2.20s. New York city gate gas tumbled several cents to the low-$2.50s.

Temperatures are expected to hover below seasonable levels throughout the mid-section of the U.S. and the Northeast this week. In the Southwest, temperatures are forecast to remain five to 10 degrees above normal in the western section but below normal in the eastern part. Warmer-than-normal weather is also continuing in the Pacific Northwest, according to Weather Services Corp.
